 Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that: That on 01022020 at about 08.35 p.m, when the petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50V5269 on Veerasagara - Byalakere Main Road, while proceeding near Race Shop Garage, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50E6183 came from opposite direction, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle and caused the accident.

As such petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately shifted to Aveksha hospital, M.S. Palya, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and discharged on 18.02.2020 with an advise to take complete bed rest and continue the medicine and to take regular followup treatment and physiotherapy and has spent huge amount towards medical and hospital charges, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and he is still under followup treatment and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 26 years and was working as Electrician at YSL Electronics, Yelahanka, Bengaluru and earning Rs.12,800/ p.m. Due to accidental injuries he is not able to do or attend his work and thereby sustained loss of income and suffering from pain and agony and mental shock and he has to undergo few more surgeries for removal of implant and corrective surgery and he has to incur huge amount towards future medical expenses.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle involved in the accident and in this regard the Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered a case against rider of the said offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of summons, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence, was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and contended that at the time of accident rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50E6183 and petitioner were not having valid and effective driving licence to ride the Motor Cycles and respondent No.1 knowing fully well that he was not having the valid and effective driving licence to ride the offending Motor Cycle and thereby they have violated the terms and conditions of the policy and at the time of accident the rider cum insured was riding the Motor Cycle under the influence of the alcohol and Police have filed Charge sheet against rider of Motor Cycle and the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50E6183 and there is delay of one day in lodging the complaint and the petitioner colluded with the insured,
hospital authorities and Police has filed a false complaint against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle in order to get compensation from this respondent and there is no valid fitness certificate to Ranganath Yadav.

2 the offending Motor Cycle at the time of accident.

This respondent admits that they have issued Policy in respect of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50E6183 vide Policy No.4215907/ 31/2019/5971 in favour of respondent No.1 and the same was valid from 25.02.2019 to 24.02.2020.
The liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further denied age,
avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is excessive, exorbitant and hence, pray to dismiss the petition against respondent No.2.
05.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:  ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 01.02.2020 at about 08.35 p.m, on Veerasagara, Byalakere Main Road, near Race Shop Garage,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the riding of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA50E6183 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03

. What Order or Award?
06.

In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and two witnesses i.e., MRI and the doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 21 documents as Ex.P.1 to 21 and closed their side evidence.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Assistant Manager got examined as RW.1 and through him 09 documents are marked as Ex.R.1 to 9 and closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as under: Issue No.1 In the Affirmative Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 09. Issue No.1:
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that the rider of another Motor Cycle had consumed alcohol and after the accident he and another rider fell down and he lost conscious and the another rider of Motor Cycle expired after the accident and admits in the Charge sheet it is stated that the rider of another Motor Cycle by consuming alcohol rode the Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and caused accident and denied to the suggestion that the wounds are healedup and admits that the outer wounds are healedup and denied to the suggestion that he has not sustained any fracture injuries and admits that the fractures are united and the doctor has issued certificate for removal of rod and denied to the suggestion that in all cases removal of rod is not Ranganath Yadav.

3 necessary and denied to the suggestion that medical bills and prescriptions are created for the purpose of this case and also stated that at the time of accident he was getting Rs.12,800/ p.m as salary and now he was getting Rs.17,000/ p.m and that for 09 months he did not attend his job and he has not produced any document to show that he could not attend his job for about 09 months and he spent nearly Rs.3,00,000/ for his medical expenses.

After discharge doctor has advised to take bed rest for one year and there is no document in this regard and denied to the suggestion that medical bills are reimbursed from ESI and denied to the suggestion that he was fit and fine as earlier without having any difficulties and denied to the suggestion that as the accident occurred due to negligence of rider of Motor Cycle by consuming alcohol, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
10. Further, the Medical Record Incharge of Aveksha hospital is examined as PW.2 and he has produced MLC register and Case sheet pertaining to the petitioner as per Ex.P.18 and 19.
During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that in Ex.P.18 only RTA by twowheeler is mentioned and he do not know the contents of documents produced by him.

11. Further, PW.3 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained distal radius fracture (volar barton's fracture), left distal 1/3rd oblique shaft of femur, left foot 2 nd metatarsal fracture with great toe phalanx fracture and he assessed permanent physical disability of 30% to left lower limb, 29% of right upper limb which is 23.3% to the whole body and he also stated that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants and he has produced OPD book and Xray films as per Ex.P.20 and 21.

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.2 counsel he stated that the fractures are united and injuries are healedup, petitioner may do his electrical works with difficulties, there is restrictions of movement and denied to the suggestion that since he has not treated doctor, he has not competent to assess disability and also stated except removal of the implants, no other future surgery is required.
In some difficulties petitioner may do his day to day work and petitioner is able to walk without any support.
12. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 21 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 21
on his behalf
. Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Yelahanka Traffic Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against rider of the offending vehicle for his rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Cycle which caused the accident.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are copy of IMV report shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Mahazar.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Sketch which indicates that the rider of offending Motor Cycle has came to extreme right side of the road and dashed the Motor Cycle of the petitioner who is in correct left side of the road.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner which indicates that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Ex.P.8 is Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted abated Charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle who also died in the accident.
On perusal of said Charge sheet, though it is mentioned that the deceased rider of the Motor Cycle was consumed the alcohol, but Sec.185 of M.V. Act is not invoked in the Charge sheet.

Further more, the percentage of alcohol has not stated and no blood report and Post mortem report or breath analysis report produced to show that the percentage of alcohol consumed by the deceased and exceed permissible limit as per Sec.185(A) of M.V. Act.

4
Ex.P.9 is copy of Aadhaar card of the petitioner.

Ex.P.10 is Discharge summary issued by Aveksha hospital, Bengaluru, which discloses that petitioner was admitted as inpatient from 02.02.2020 and discharged on 18.02.2020 for 16 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.16 is Xrays.
Ex.P.18 is MLC register.
Ex.P.19 is Case sheet.
Ex.P.20 is OPD book and Ex.P.21 is Xray films.

13. Further, to disprove the case of the petitioner, the Assistant Manager of the respondent No.2 is examined as RW.1, wherein in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments.
During the cross examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force.
14. Further, the RW.1 has produced Ex.R.1 is Authorization letter.

Ex.R.2 is copy of Policy issued by the respondent No.2 pertaining to the offending Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50E6183 which indicates that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending Motor Cycle was valid and is in force subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Ex.R.3 is copy of letter issued to insured.
Ex.R.4 is Postal receipt having prooof of sending the said notice to the owner.
Ex.R.5 is Unserved RPAD cover with letter.
Ex.R.6 is copy of letter issued to insured wife.
Ex.R.7 is Postal receipt.
Ex.R.8 is Unserved RPAD cover with letter and Ex.R.9 is copy of Charge sheet.

15. In this case the main contention of the Insurance Company is that the rider of the Motor Cycle was riding the offending Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol and Police have filed Charge sheet, policy terms and conditions are violated, hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It is true that as per Ex.P.8 and Ex.R.9 Charge sheet, Police have mentioned that the deceased rider of the offending Motor Cycle was riding the Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol.
But the Investigation Officer has not invoked the provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act for drunk and drive.

Further, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company or Investigation Officer have not produced the proof of analysis report or blood test report or Post mortem report of deceased rider to show the percentage of alcohol consumed by the deceased rider.

As per Sec.185(A)
of M.V. Act, it says that driving by a drunken person has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser
, then only it is Sec.185 of M.V. Act can be attracted.
Therefore, the rider of the offending Motor Cycle consumed alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood detected in a test smell by the deceased rider of the Motor Cycle is not proved.

Only mere mentioning of under the influence of alcohol in the Charge sheet without mentioning provisions, creates doubt regarding the rider of the offending Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol has riding the Motor Cycle as on the date of accident.

Moreover, even the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has not made any attempt to produce Post mortem report of the deceased which may shows whether the deceased rider of the Motor Cycle was consumed alcohol or not.
Therefore, in the absence of cogent, believable and clinching evidence regarding the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was riding the Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol is not proved.

Therefore, on perusal of above oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that the he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 01022020 at about 08.35 p.m, on Veerasagara - Byalakere Main Road, near Race Shop Garage, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of riding of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA50 E6183 by its rider as alleged in the petition.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved the Issue No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

5 16.
Issue No.2:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 26 years and was working as Electrician and earning Rs.12,800/ p.m and has incurred huge amount towards medical and hospital charges, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and due to accidental injuries he suffered loss of income, pain and sufferings and became permanent disabled.

17. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and he has not produced any evidence regarding his avocation and income.
But he has produced Ex.P.9 and 12 Aadhaar card and driving licence, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 21.02.1995 and the alleged accident occurred on 01022020.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 25 years and the same is considered for calculating compensation.
As per Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is 18 and the same is considered.
18. As discussed above, with regard to avocation and income the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the LokAdalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2020 to be taken as Rs.14,500/ p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.14,500/.
19.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained distal radius fracture (volar barton's fracture), left distal 1/3rd oblique shaft of femur, left foot 2nd metatarsal fracture with great toe phalanx fracture and he assessed permanent physical disability of 30% to left lower limb, 29% of right upper limb which is 23.3% to the whole body.
However, considering the evidence of PW.3 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 20%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.10 Discharge summary, according to which the petitioner was admitted to Aveksha hospital as inpatient for 16 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges,
he is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.
21. Pain and sufferings: As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and Ex.P.18 MLC register.
Ex.P.19 Case sheet.
Ex . P.20
OPD book and Ex.P.21 Xray films and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.

6 22.
Loss of income during laid up period:

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.14,500/ p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 16 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.29,000/
(Rs.14,500 x 2) under this head.
23. Medical expenses:
As per Ex.P.14 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.3,81,036/. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,81,036/ under the head of medical expenses.
24. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
25. Future medical expenses:

According to PW.3 doctor the radiological examination shows fractures united with implants in situ right radius and left femur and also stated petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
The petitioner has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.

26. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 6,26,40000 2.
Pain and
Sufferings 30,00000
3. Attendant charges, extra 30,00000 nutritious food and conveyance charges 4.
Medical Expenses 3,81,03600 5. Loss of future amenities in 30,00000 life and unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 29,00000 period 7.
Future medical expenses 30,00000 Total 11,56,43600 27.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.11,56,436/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/) from the date of petition till its realization.

7 28.

As discussed supra, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has taken contention that the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was riding the Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol and caused accident and violated the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
As per Ex.P.8 and Ex.R.9 Charge sheet, though there is a mention of rider of the offending Motor Cycle was riding the Motor Cycle was consuming alcohol.
But the Investigation Officer has not invoked the provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act.
The owner cum rider of the offending Motor Cycle was died in the accident.
Even if it is proved that deceased rider of Motor Cycle consumed alcohol and caused accident, then also Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation to the third parties.
Ex.R.2 is copy of Policy of the offending Motor Cycle.
From a bare look at the conditions contained in the policy, drunk and drive exonerated the Insurance Company from personal accident cover of the owner and driver, but not the third parties.

The conditions specified under the policy with regard to liability to pay compensation for third party risk and driving the vehicle by the driver of the vehicle in drunken state would not exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.

However, Insurance Company is not liable when the vehicle was driven by driver in drunken state, in view of the terms and conditions extracted above,
in personal injury claims perhaps, the third party is not supposed to know about the intoxicated state of driver, when he was proceeding on the road.
Therefore, policy conditions did not exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation to third parties, though the vehicle was driven by a driver in drunken state.
29. U/Sec 185 of M.V. Act the permissible limit is only 30 mg. per 100 ml. Blood.

Even if there is any condition, that driving of a vehicle in intoxicated condition is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, Still the Insurance Company is liable for payment of compensation.
Drunk and driving is not a ground to avoid liability to exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.
The Insurance Company would still remain liable to innocent third parties otherwise award obtained by the petitioner in this case only remain paper award.

In the case on hand Investigation Officer has not invoked provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act and no breath analyser report or blood test report has been produced to prove the exceeding limit of intoxication of the deceased of the Motor Cycle and no Post mortem report has been produced to prove the intoxication of alcohol by the deceased rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
As per Ex.R.2 the policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid from 25.02.2019 to 24.02.2020.
The alleged accident occurred on 01.02.2020.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 since deceased, his LR wife being the owner of the offending Motor Cycle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.11,56,436/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/) to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount with interest from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

8

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,56,436/ (Rupees Eleven lakhs fifty six thousand four hundred and thirty six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through Epayment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
15. In this case the main contention of the Insurance Company is that the rider of the Motor Cycle was riding the offending Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol and Police have filed Charge sheet, policy terms and conditions are violated, hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
But the Investigation Officer has not invoked the provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act for drunk and drive.
Further, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company or Investigation Officer have not produced the proof of analysis report or blood test report or Post mortem report of deceased rider to show the percentage of alcohol consumed by the deceased rider.
As per Sec.185(A)
of M.V. Act, it says that driving by a drunken person has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser
, then only it is Sec.185 of M.V. Act can be attracted.
Therefore, the rider of the offending Motor Cycle consumed alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood detected in a test smell by the deceased rider of the Motor Cycle is not proved.
Only mere mentioning of under the influence of alcohol in the Charge sheet without mentioning provisions, creates doubt regarding the rider of the offending Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol has riding the Motor Cycle as on the date of accident.
Moreover, even the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has not made any attempt to produce Post mortem report of the deceased which may shows whether the deceased rider of the Motor Cycle was consumed alcohol or not.
Therefore, in the absence of cogent, believable and clinching evidence regarding the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was riding the Motor Cycle under the influence of alcohol is not proved.
The owner cum rider of the offending Motor Cycle was died in the accident.
Even if it is proved that deceased rider of Motor Cycle consumed alcohol and caused accident, then also Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation to the third parties.
From a bare look at the conditions contained in the policy, drunk and drive exonerated the Insurance Company from personal accident cover of the owner and driver, but not the third parties.
The conditions specified under the policy with regard to liability to pay compensation for third party risk and driving the vehicle by the driver of the vehicle in drunken state would not exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.
However, Insurance Company is not liable when the vehicle was driven by driver in drunken state, in view of the terms and conditions extracted above,
in personal injury claims perhaps, the third party is not supposed to know about the intoxicated state of driver, when he was proceeding on the road.
Therefore, policy conditions did not exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation to third parties, though the vehicle was driven by a driver in drunken state.
Even if there is any condition, that driving of a vehicle in intoxicated condition is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, Still the Insurance Company is liable for payment of compensation.
Drunk and driving is not a ground to avoid liability to exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.
The Insurance Company would still remain liable to innocent third parties otherwise award obtained by the petitioner in this case only remain paper award.
In the case on hand Investigation Officer has not invoked provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act and no breath analyser report or blood test report has been produced to prove the exceeding limit of intoxication of the deceased of the Motor Cycle and no Post mortem report has been produced to prove the intoxication of alcohol by the deceased rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
The alleged accident occurred on 01.02.2020.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force.
